findings.claim: The de-dup search pipeline at lines 424-431 ends with | head -1 after the jq filter. With set -euo pipefail in effect and the whole pipeline inside a command substitution existing="$(...)", a SIGPIPE scenario is possible: if the jq filter ever emits 2+ issue numbers and head -1 terminates after consuming the first line, the gh issue list process receives SIGPIPE and exits non-zero; pipefail then causes the command substitution to exit non-zero; set -e aborts the step before the issue-create or issue-comment branch executes, silently dropping the alert. The canary-replay.yml de-dup at line 127 avoids this by using --jq '.[0].number // empty' (first-element selection entirely within jq, no external pipe), which exits 0 regardless of result count. In the release-gate scenario, 2+ exact-title matches for the same tag require multiple unresolved failures of the same tag cut, making this edge case near-impossible in practice, but the pattern divergence from the established canary-replay.yml approach is a latent correctness risk for future maintainers extending the de-dup window or increasing result volume.
findings.evidence: release-gate.yml lines 424-431: --json number,title --jq ".[] | select(.title == \"${title}\") | .number" | head -1 inside existing="$(...)"; canary-replay.yml line 127: --jq '.[0].number // empty' (no external pipe); bash manual — pipefail: the exit status of a pipeline is the exit status of the last command that exited with a non-zero status, or zero if all commands exited successfully; POSIX SIGPIPE — when head terminates and the producer writes to the broken pipe, producer receives SIGPIPE and typically exits non-zero unless it catches/ignores SIGPIPE; git commit 63ba1ea applies the R1 COR-nit-001 fix that introduced head -1 (not present in the prior canary-replay.yml pattern).
findings.impact: In the realistic operational scenario (0-1 matching issues per tag), the pipeline never has 2+ outputs and head -1 is a no-op; pipefail risk is zero. In the degenerate scenario (2+ exact-title open issues for the same tag), the step aborts without opening or commenting on any issue — a silent alert drop on a workflow run that already represents a compliance failure. The label-ensure step before this step will have already succeeded, leaving the labels present but no issue created or updated.
findings.mitigation: Replace --json number,title --jq ".[] | select(.title == \"${title}\") | .number" | head -1 with a single-jq expression: --json number,title --jq "first(.[] | select(.title == \"${title}\") | .number) // empty". The first(expr) idiom evaluates only until the first match and exits, eliminating the external pipe and the SIGPIPE failure path. This is the exact pattern analogue of canary-replay.yml's .[0].number // empty, adapted for the select-based exact-title matching that distinguishes release-gate de-dup from canary-replay de-dup. No logic change.
